tools.name: fluxproof_preflight
tools.description: Fetch a public URL and return fetchability, size, final URL, title, and content hash without page content or payment. Start here before creating a monitor. Example: {"url":"https://example.com/"}.

tools.name: fluxproof_offer
tools.description: Return free and paid boundaries and purchase routes without charging. Read this for the free daily plan, $9 paid pass, human checkout and agent payment route. Example: {}. A returned offer is not purchase authorization.

tools.name: fluxproof_create_monitor
tools.description: Create a monitor using a buyer-owned FluxProof API key. Creates persistent state and performs a baseline check, consuming quota. Not idempotent; do not retry blindly after an uncertain result.

tools.name: fluxproof_check_now
tools.description: Run a monitor now and return a source- and hash-bound change receipt. Consumes check quota, stores a receipt and may deliver a configured webhook. Not an idempotent read.

tools.name: fluxproof_list_changes
tools.description: List recent evidence receipts for a monitor.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "fluxproof_offer" references sensitive artifacts (authorization). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: fluxproof_preflight · Private data: fluxproof_create_monitor · Public sink: fluxproof_check_now · Destructive: fluxproof_check_now.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: fluxproof_preflight · Private data: fluxproof_create_monitor · Public sink: fluxproof_check_now · Destructive: fluxproof_check_now

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "fluxproof_preflight" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Fetch a public URL and return fetchability, size, final URL, title, and content hash without page content or payment." → after: "Fetch a public URL and return fetchability, size, final URL, title, and content hash without page content or payment. Start here before creating a monitor. Example: {"url":"https://example.com/"}."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
